title: ReseedBarn struct @dev 'fertilizerIds MUST be in acsending order' is never enforced in mintFertilizers, allowing a malformed nextFid linked list
description: The Fertilizers struct NatSpec (line 34) states a hard requirement using 'MUST': '@dev fertilizerIds MUST be in acsending order.' mintFertilizers builds the fertilizer linked list relying on this order: it sets s.sys.fert.fertFirst on i==0, s.sys.fert.nextFid[fertilizerIds[i-1].fertilizerId] = fid for i!=0, and s.sys.fert.fertLast on the last element. No require or comparison enforces that f.fertilizerId values are strictly ascending. If the upgrade input is out of order (or contains duplicate ids), the nextFid mapping is wired incorrectly — producing a chain that skips ids, points backward, or forms a cycle — while fertFirst/fertLast are taken from positional (not value) extremes. The documented invariant is stated with 'MUST' but enforced only by trust in the caller's input ordering.
impact: A non-ascending or duplicate-id input yields a malformed/cyclic fertilizer linked list. Sun fertilizer payout traverses nextFid in id order to pay Beans to fertilizer holders; a corrupted chain strands or mispays fertilizer (holders past the break never get paid, or a cycle disrupts iteration). Bounded by trusted upgrade-caller input, hence Medium per Immunefi v2.2 (incorrect protocol behavior / griefing of payouts rather than directly attacker-permissionless).

ite.intent: Stated intent ('MUST be ascending'): build a correctly ordered ascending fertilizer linked list.
ite.technique: Ordering enforced by NatSpec comment only; no require/comparison on consecutive fertilizerId values.
ite.evasion: No attacker; depends on upgrade-caller input correctness — a documented invariant left structurally unguarded.
